# Results summary — Korean sentiment: neural vs TF-IDF crossover

*Generated by `python -m ksent.analysis.make_summary` from `source/results/` (same macros as the report).*

## Answer to the research question

**No crossover up to 8,000 reviews on any dataset.** The best neural model never beats the best TF-IDF
model by ≥ 1.0 macro-F1 point at any size (winners selected on validation; the test-selected
sensitivity check agrees: none up to 8,000 / none up to 8,000 / none up to 8,000).

| Dataset | Threshold | Winners at 8k (TF-IDF vs neural) | Gap @500 (pts) | Gap @8k (pts) | Fit time ratio | CPU latency ratio | RAM ratio | Neural Pareto-efficient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NSMC (movies) | none up to 8,000 | TF-IDF + SVM vs Emb + BiGRU | -4.71 ± 1.24 | -0.48 ± 0.49 | 54.4× | 1.2× | 1.6× | no |
| Shopping | none up to 8,000 | TF-IDF + SVM vs Emb + BiLSTM | -4.60 ± 0.58 | -0.49 ± 0.39 | 61.3× | 1.4× | 1.7× | no |
| Steam (games) | none up to 8,000 | TF-IDF + LR vs Emb + MLP | -5.92 ± 1.57 | -1.12 ± 0.24 | 11.4× | 0.7× | 1.6× | yes |

Gap = neural − TF-IDF, paired per seed, mean ± sample std over 5 seeds. Ratios = neural / TF-IDF winner at
n = 8,000 (exclusive cost runs). Steam's neural winner is Pareto-efficient only via slightly lower CPU latency
(0.826 vs 1.165 ms); it is less accurate, slower to fit and uses more RAM.

## Key numbers (test macro-F1 ×100, n = 8,000)

- Best overall: NSMC TF-IDF + SVM 83.50 ± 0.00; Shopping TF-IDF + SVM 90.45 ± 0.00; Steam TF-IDF + LR 75.95 ± 0.00.
- Best neural (val-selected): NSMC Emb + BiGRU 83.02 ± 0.49; Shopping Emb + BiLSTM 89.96 ± 0.39; Steam Emb + MLP 74.83 ± 0.24.
- Mamba (weakest neural, `torch_ref` backend): 78.81 ± 0.87 / 87.20 ± 0.44 / 73.22 ± 0.63.
- Gap closes with data but no method saturates: last doubling (4k→8k) adds 2.05 ± 0.39 / 1.28 ± 0.37 /
  1.62 ± 0.48 points for the TF-IDF winner and 3.14 ± 0.89 / 2.32 ± 0.59 /
  2.49 ± 0.47 for the neural winner (NSMC / Shopping / Steam).
- Test OOV rate of the neural vocabulary: 20.5% / 16.6% / 18.6% at n = 500 →
  5.9% / 4.2% / 5.1% at n = 8,000 (plausible cause of the weak neural start).
- Deterministic models (TF-IDF + LR/SVM) have std = 0 at n = 8,000 (every seed uses the full pool).
  Five seeds measure variability; they are not a significance test.

## Tokenizer ablation verdict

The conclusion holds under each family's best (validation-selected) tokenizer. Gap at n = 8,000: NSMC: -0.48 ± 0.49 (best tokenizers TF-IDF Kiwi, neural Kiwi; holds: yes); Shopping: 0.77 ± 0.39 (best tokenizers TF-IDF character, neural Kiwi; holds: yes); Steam: -1.12 ± 0.24 (best tokenizers TF-IDF Kiwi, neural Kiwi; holds: yes).
Kiwi morphemes are best for both families almost everywhere; eojeol is clearly worst. On Shopping at 8k validation
picks character TF-IDF, which is worse on test, so the gap turns positive but stays below 1.0 point.

## Compute used

One machine: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (1 GPU), AMD EPYC 7C13 64-Core Processor, fp32, 8 threads per TF-IDF job,
2 per neural job; quality stages ran 4 GPU jobs + 6 CPU jobs concurrently,
cost stages one job at a time.

| Stage | Mode | Runs | Busy wall (h) | Mean GPU util | Mean CPU util (of 128 logical) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C pilot | cost | 18 | 0.17 | 27% | 2.7% |
| D tuning | cost | 270 | 1.65 | 22% | 2.8% |
| E main sweep | quality | 675 | 1.54 | 88% | 6.4% |
| F ablation | quality | 120 | 0.12 | 75% | 7.5% |
| G cost pass | cost | 135 | 1.72 | 27% | 3.1% |

Total busy wall time 5.2 h = 5.2 GPU-hours on one GPU (8.8 h of summed
neural-job time). Busy wall excludes waiting for exclusivity (the pilot first waited for unrelated GPU jobs to finish).

## Result counts, failures and anomalies

- Tuning fits 270 / 270, quality fits 795 (main 675 / 675 +
  ablation 120 / 120), cost fits 135 / 135; crossover-size cost fits: 0
  (no crossover). Every dataset × method × size has 5 valid seeds.
- **Failures: 0** (`source/results/failed.jsonl` is empty); no retries were needed.
- Determinism: 135 / 135 cost runs reproduce their quality-mode test predictions exactly
  (max disagreement 0.0%), for classical and GPU-trained models alike.
- Container restart at 05:44 UTC interrupted tuning at 100/270; resumed without redoing finished fits.
- Scheduler bottleneck in the first 19 min of the main sweep (one job at a time); fixed (scheduling only, predictions
  unaffected), 4 in-flight fits discarded and rerun.
- High seed variance at n = 500 for Steam LSTM / Transformer (one or two poorly trained seeds); reported, not removed.
- Deviations: Python 3.12 instead of 3.11 (pinned numpy 2.5.4 needs ≥ 3.12); Mamba uses the `torch_ref` backend (no
  mamba-ssm wheel for torch 2.14); 5 seeds instead of 3; tokenizer ablation added; costs measured at n = 8,000 only.
